name: Oshokuya Kappa (京都イタリアン 欧食屋Kappa)

claims.text: Restaurant states 'コンタミの可能性があるので、小麦アレルギーに対応はしておりません' — cross-contamination is possible, so they do not formally accommodate a wheat allergy, despite the kitchen using no wheat flour.
Homepage repeats they serve gluten-free dishes with no wheat flour but explicitly '小麦アレルギーに対応はしておりません' due to contamination risk (likely supplier/seasoning-level).
The restaurant openly declines to guarantee safety for a medical wheat allergy (小麦アレルギー未対応) even while marketing itself as fully gluten-free; strict celiacs should self-identify and confirm.
Kitchen converted entirely to gluten-free in Sept 2024, using no wheat flour; wheat pasta and focaccia were replaced with house-made rice-flour pasta and 米粉パン.
Curated Japanese GF guide rates it ★★★★★ with 'all menu items gluten-free' (すべてのメニューがグルテンフリー).
Signature 50-vegetable gluten-free course by a certified vegetable sommelier.

Dedicated gluten-free facility: the entire product line is made with rice flour (米粉) and no wheat flour is used anywhere, so there is no wheat in the production environment to cross-contaminate. Own claim: 「グルテン、卵、乳製品、白砂糖を使わず、米粉で作ったスイーツ」.
Not applicable — this is a sweets-only maker; no soy sauce or savory wheat-containing seasonings are involved. Products use organic soy milk and organic maple syrup, not wheat-based ingredients.
Fully vegan facility — no eggs or dairy are used in any product (casein-free), so there is no animal-product cross-contact risk in the kitchen.

The brand was founded specifically for people avoiding wheat/gluten, dairy and eggs, and markets its sweets as suitable for those with wheat allergy and following gluten-free/casein-free diets; gift and mail-order packaging is a core part of the business.

Whole facility is gluten-free AND vegan by design — no wheat, egg, dairy or white sugar anywhere, using 特別栽培の米粉, 有機豆乳 and オーガニックメープルシロップ; colors come from natural ingredients with no artificial colorants.
Entirely wheat-free kitchen - no wheat flour is used anywhere, and the signature bread is 100% rice flour with no binders, so wheat cross-contamination risk is minimal.

The specific soy sauce/seasoning brand is not documented online. Since the kitchen is fully gluten-free, the seasonings are presumably wheat-free, but a celiac-level diner should confirm a tamari (wheat-free) shoyu is used.
The entire operation is 100% vegan with no animal products handled, so there is no risk of animal-based cross-contact.
The shop explicitly caters to people with food allergies as part of its core mission, and the chef has years of experience making gluten-free, allergy-conscious foods.

Fully vegan AND fully gluten-free dedicated kitchen - no meat, fish, dairy, eggs, or wheat, plus no chemical seasonings or refined white sugar - making it one of the safer choices in Kyoto for both vegan and GF travelers.
小麦粉は完全不使用で、米粉やアーモンドの粉などを使用。工房全体がグルテンフリー専用のため小麦の混入リスクは構造的に極めて低い。
「卵・乳製品・小麦・白砂糖不使用、ヴィーガン＆グルテンフリーのお菓子」と全商品を明記。
スイーツ専門店のため醤油・味噌など小麦を含む発酵調味料は使用しない。該当なし。
工房全体が完全ヴィーガンで卵・乳製品を一切扱わないため、動物性食材との交差接触リスクはない。
店主はカフェ商品開発時に食物アレルギーを研究し、3大アレルゲン不使用スイーツの製造販売から創業。アレルギー対応が事業の中核。
小麦を一切扱わない完全グルテンフリー＆ヴィーガンの菓子工房で、全商品が対象。添加物も「できる限り使いません」。
全国にファンを持つ人気店で通販実績も豊富。長野駅善光寺口から徒歩数分とアクセス良好。
「工房内では一切小麦を使わない、三大アレルゲンフリーの丸パン」 — the workshop uses no wheat at all; rolls are free of the three major allergens.
「小麦は一切持ち込まないアレルギー対応の専用工房」— a dedicated allergy-response workshop into which wheat is never brought; products labeled アレルギー28品目対応.
Bakery/sweets shop with no wheat on premises; wheat-based soy sauce is not a relevant ingredient here, and the workshop is wheat-free by policy.

Egg and dairy ARE used in some products (scones use 平飼い卵; chiffon/canelé/あんバター contain egg or butter), so vegan and egg/dairy-allergic visitors must read labels even though the shop is fully wheat-free.

Shop manager Misari Yamaguchi has a personal wheat-intolerance background and trained at a gluten-free café; founder Itaru Inoue started the sorghum business for his wheat-allergic son — allergy safety is core to the shop's purpose.
Dedicated gluten-free specialty shop marketed as safe for wheat-allergic children, with items labeled to Japan's 28-allergen standard (アレルギー28品目対応) and 卵・乳・小麦不使用 options.
Confirmed open (opened 8 April 2023); Tabelog rating 3.00, address 長野県長野市若里2-1-23, phone 026-466-6610.

All food is rice-flour based with no wheat flour used, so baking cross-contact risk is low; bottled beer/sparkling wine on premises is the main gluten source and should be kept away from a celiac's food.
Sweets café; no soy-sauce-based savoury dishes at time of research (planned rice-bread light meals not yet confirmed).
Cakes use eggs and dairy; no dedicated vegan prep noted.
Featured on a wheat-allergy blogger's Matsumoto gluten-free tour as a GF café; owner intends the shop as a safe rice-flour space.
Entire sweets menu is gluten-free and white-sugar-free using Nagano rice flour.

name: Riz Karuizawa (リズ カルイザワ)

claims.text: Dedicated rice-flour bakery — no wheat flour used on premises, so cross-contact risk is very low.
Breads use 米粉 (Koshihikari rice flour) with 白神こだま酵母; some also blend 大豆粉 (soy flour), which is gluten-free.
Range includes meat (bacon ears, wiener roll) and egg bakes (chiffon); an allergen card for milk/soy is posted — confirm per item.
Allergen reference board (food/milk) available in-store.
100% rice-flour, gluten-free bakery; listed as a gluten-free bakery on FindMeGlutenFree for Karuizawa.
Owner states all products are gluten-free (全商品グルテンフリー), uses no wheat flour, and mills her own rice — an effectively wheat-free kitchen; confirm no shared equipment.
Bakery/tea room; no soy-sauce savoury cooking noted.
Some bakes use butter, egg, or ham-and-cheese; not all items vegan.
Owner is herself gluten-free and built the shop for gluten-free customers; takeout requires an advance phone reservation.
All products gluten-free and white-sugar-free; owner-celiac dedicated rice-flour bakery.
